newsitem.title: ITALY: Van Miert says IRI debt extension not ruled out.
newsitem.headline: Van Miert says IRI debt extension not ruled out.

text.p: European Commissioner Karel van Miert indicated Italian state industrial holding IRI could be granted a further extension to a deadline on cutting its debt to levels agreed with the EU Commission.

Van Miert, speaking on the fringe of a telecommunications conference here, said based on specific undertakings by the Italian government, the Commission "will assess whether to allow IRI a few more months extension" to bring its debt down.
The Commission has given the Italian government until the end of June to cut IRI debt down to below five trillion lire ($2.9 billion).
IRI said last month its net financial indebtedness had fallen to 9.4 trillion lire at the end of 1996 from 22.5 trillion previously.

Van Miert said he hoped the privatisation of Italian motorway manager Autostrade, which is controlled by IRI, would take place at the expected time and noted that in the past he had to work hard to convince the Commission to grant IRI an extension of six months.
IRI had been given a previous deadline for the end of 1996 and Van Miert had previously ruled out any further extension of the deadline.
